world_3d_rendered_triage.pause_menu_root_cause: GTA SA pauses itself and opens the pause menu whenever its window loses activation. Opening another Chrome window in front of the game window paused the guest, so every world frame carried the menu. Emulation.setFocusEmulationEnabled keeps the document focused for the guest regardless of the window manager, and with it the intro cutscene runs unpaused.
world_3d_rendered_triage.queued_input_root_cause: A mouse click dispatched to the menu stays in the guest input queue while the game streams assets and is replayed once gameplay starts, where the game reads it as Start and opens the pause menu. Menu navigation therefore uses Enter only, verified against a screenshot crop of the menu row band.

fixes: dx/d3d9_ffp.cpp: diffuse fixed-function lighting synthesized in vertex_program, emissive + ambient * D3DRS_AMBIENT + sum(light.diffuse * material.diffuse * max(0, N.L)), with the normal rotated to world space by c8..c11 and normalized. Alpha is written separately and never lit.

target.arithmetic: At 22.9 FPS the frame lasts 43.7 ms and the guest thread spends 43.6% of it (~19.0 ms) in translated guest code alone, against the 16.7 ms budget of a 60 FPS frame. runtime/kernel32.cpp: sched_wait_locked clock reads are guarded by perf_stats::on(), and SCHED_SLICE_SECONDS goes from 0.001 to 0.004.

root_causes: The translator computed fn.seh_restores in prepare() and never consulted it: the rule that emits recomp_seh_frame_leave for MOV FS:[0], reg was gated on fn.seh_sites, which is empty for the epilogue block body_004835cc because its prologue lives in another recovered block. Address 0x004835ef therefore emitted no leave, so fn_00481300 installed 845 SEH frames and retired none.

The runtime retire predicate was registration < ESP, which cannot fire for this MSVC epilogue shape: it loads the chain head from [ESP+0x1fc] into ECX and pops only part of the frame, leaving ESP below the registration.

stage_lock allocated a full-resource staging block on the first Lock and stage_unlock copied and freed it on the last, so a game that locks a dynamic buffer once per draw paid an allocation, two copies and a free per draw. gpu_after_unlock additionally marked the whole buffer dirty, so every draw re-uploaded the entire vertex or index buffer.
fixes: tools/recomp/translate.py: the MOV rule now consults fn.seh_restores with a seh_unproven_establishment guard so a body whose establishment could not be proven is not retired. Emissions of recomp_seh_frame_leave go from 6 to 563.

runtime/seh.cpp: frame liveness is decided by membership in the guest SEH chain, the same test recomp_seh_resume_frame already applied, with a bounded prune_unlinked_frames net (one pass every 1024 resumptions and only above 32 live frames). recomp_callback_depth() is hoisted out of the scan loop.

dx/d3d9.cpp and dx/com.h: the staging block survives the lock (stage_bytes) for vertex and index buffers only; a texture frees it on unlock so a second full image is not held per texture for the whole session. Unlock uploads only the locked range, widened outward to a four-byte multiple because the backend write offset must be aligned.
reverted_experiments: Implementing os_monotonic_ns with emscripten_get_now() instead of clock_gettime: _emscripten_get_now rose from 9.6% to 28.7% of the guest thread in the profile. Reverted on that direct measurement.

Reading the scheduler checkpoint clock once every 16 calls: first rejected on a comparison that was invalid because the two sides were sampled at different points of asset loading (frames 8101-9601 against 11101-12601). Re-measured with the stable protocol (settle 340 s, read the tail STAT reports) it gives 19.1 FPS against 18.6-19.6 without the change, so it is within noise and was dropped for adding scheduler latency without a measurable gain.

Lesson recorded for later rounds: frame rate figures are only comparable between runs that reach the same point of the scene, which is why the protocol settles 340 s and discards the loading-phase reports.

root_cause_measured_this_round.the_guest_is_not_sleeping: The runtime's own sampler (RECOMP_PROFILE=1, RECOMP_PROFILE_INTERVAL_MS=2000) samples the baton holder at 1 kHz and counts a sample idle when that thread is not inside a translated function. Across about 45 two-second windows during gameplay: 24 windows at 0.0-1.5% idle, 15 at 1.6-3.9%, 6 at 4.6-6.9%. The guest executes translated code 93-100% of the time.
root_cause_measured_this_round.hypothesis_this_rejects: The round opened on the hypothesis that GTA SA's own default 30 FPS frame limiter was sleeping the guest and that the CPU therefore had about 2x of headroom. It does not: there is no idle time to reclaim.

what_the_time_is_actually_spent_on.FUN_00561a80: 20-30% of sampled time. Eight instructions: reads an imported function pointer, calls it, subtracts a time base. This is the shape of CTimer::GetTimeInMilliseconds.
what_the_time_is_actually_spent_on.FUN_00748710.blk_00748da0: 25-45% of sampled time. A loop that calls Sleep(0x64) and reads the clock.

root_cause_measured_this_round.the_limiter_spins_instead_of_sleeping: The kit already documented this: runtime/kernel32.cpp:1715 says "this game's frame limiter spins here" and :2054 says "the frame limiter's GetTickCount spin is left alone". GTA San Andreas paces frames by calling GetTickCount in a loop until its deadline passes; it does not Sleep.

fixes: vendor/recomp-kit/CMakeLists.txt: -fwasm-exceptions and -sSUPPORT_LONGJMP=wasm are applied globally for EMSCRIPTEN targets. With the JavaScript setjmp/longjmp, any indirect call in a unit that can throw compiles to an invoke_* import, a wasm -> JS -> wasm round trip that copies arguments and rebuilds the frame; the translated guest dispatches every call through a function pointer, so that wrapper sat on tens of thousands of calls per frame. The shipped wasm now has 0 invoke_* imports out of 331, and V8 compiles the whole module.

vendor/recomp-kit/CMakeLists.txt, runtime/, dx/, host/, host/gpu/, mods/: the five per-target -fno-exceptions blocks from the previous round were removed. They were a detour that left the 26 invoke_* in place, because Emscripten's JS SJLJ emits them regardless of the C++ exception setting.

runtime/imports.cpp: the per-page watchdog histogram and the per-trampoline call counter now sit behind import_stats_on(), true only with RECOMP_WATCHDOG_TLS or RECOMP_WATCHDOG_CS. Both were unconditional stores into shared memory on a path that runs about a million times a second, and neither is read without those switches.
runtime/imports.cpp: log_level() is read once into a static const int verbose inside imports_dispatch instead of being called per dispatch.
reverted_experiments: -sGROWABLE_ARRAYBUFFERS=2, which the linker recommends for -pthread + ALLOW_MEMORY_GROWTH and which would address exactly the non-wasm slowness that bounds this build. It breaks the WebGPU backend: "Uncaught TypeError: Failed to execute 'setBindGroup' on GPURenderPassEncoder: The provided ArrayBuffer value must not be resizable".

Serving the guest's millisecond clock from the monotonic reads the scheduler already takes (host_publish_millis, about a million reads/s without a host call). Measured neutral, 23.96 FPS against 23.84, and reverted: in wasm os_monotonic_ns() is not the trip into JS that the clock counter suggested, so the saving did not justify touching the time path.

Scaling the guest clock 2x to separate "out of CPU" from "waiting for its own limiter". The game hangs in the menu because its fade logic depends on real time, so the experiment answers nothing. Reverted with the clock cache.
browser_performance_triage_frame_limiter.corrected_claim: The previous round's section states that 60 FPS is out of reach "with arithmetic" because translated code alone already costs ~19 ms of the 16.7 ms budget. That figure remains consistent, but the conclusion is NOT established: the split came from a profile that attributed time by worker samples, which read as 97% in __pthread_cond_timedwait, while the baton sampler that measures the thread actually executing reports 0-7% idle. The dominant share of what that profile called translated code is a wait loop on the clock (CTimer::GetTimeInMilliseconds), not simulation work, and it is exactly the part the kit already knows how to replace. 60 FPS is neither demonstrated nor ruled out.

next_step_identified.what: Wire the audited frame-limiter substitution: native_frame_clock() in runtime/kernel32.cpp:1665 retires both draw-loop deadlines and lets the kit pace frames through mods_display_fps().
next_step_identified.why_it_is_not_done: It only compiles when the variant defines RECOMP_HOOK_FRAME_CLOCK_BEGIN, _WAIT, _WAIT_CLAMP, _CLAMP_DEADLINE and _WAIT_DEADLINE, and variants/singleplayer/game.toml has no [hooks] section, so in this build that path is dead code and the game's limiter spins untouched.
next_step_identified.what_it_needs: Auditing the five addresses. The comment at kernel32.cpp:1660 names 0049cfc0 (deadline begin; it selects the second wait when game-state 2 has frame-rate flags) and 0049cfe0 (the default 60, or 24/20/14 Hz limit), and records that neither deadline drives simulation (004a5590 uses 005cd92c/005cd930 and the real clock). The two waits and the two deadline addresses are unconfirmed, and they were not wired from guesswork: a wrong address does not fail, it silently changes the game's pacing.

the_game_never_imports_GetTickCount.substitution_is_unreachable: native_frame_clock() in runtime/kernel32.cpp is keyed on k_GetTickCount: it compares each call's return address against the five RECOMP_HOOK_FRAME_CLOCK_* values. The pinned executable never reaches it.
evidence: The generated translation contains no call to GetTickCount; the string does not occur in build/recomp/gen.
The game's clock is QueryPerformanceCounter through the IAT slot at 0x008580c8; FUN_00561a80 reads that counter and subtracts the base at 0x00b7cb38.

A diagnostic (RECOMP_TICK_CALLERS) that histogrammed the return address of every GetTickCount call recorded zero calls across two gameplay runs, while the same build reported 92k-560k clock reads per second through the QPC path.
the_game_never_imports_GetTickCount.diagnostic_removed: The histogram was removed before the final artifact: it can never fire for this executable, so it was unverifiable code rather than a tool.

the_addresses_in_that_comment_were_wrong.0049cfe0: Not a draw wait. FUN_0049cfe0, 72 instructions, is a bounding-box test over the entity list at 0x00a9ad70, called with two arguments from chunk_021.c:3524 and :3557, with float compares.
the_addresses_in_that_comment_were_wrong.0049cfc0: Not a function entry: it lies inside FUN_0049cec0 (78 instructions).
the_addresses_in_that_comment_were_wrong.why_this_mattered: Wiring those addresses would not have failed. It would have changed game pacing silently, which is why they were not wired.

measurement.scene: The same Los Santos alley; one 70 s run plus earlier runs at the same point.
measurement.method: The shim's STAT d3d9 lines every 300 presented frames, read from window.recompLog; plus the runtime sampler RECOMP_PROFILE=1 with RECOMP_PROFILE_INTERVAL_MS=2000. Gameplay confirmed by draws > 100 before any number is trusted.

why_this_rules_out_a_limiter: fps sits at 24.2-24.4 between 430 and 888 draws. If per-draw cost were the binding constraint, 430 would have to be far above 888.

The baton-holder sampler reports 1-4 idle samples out of 130-131 per 2 s window (about 1-3%), and spreads the rest over many guest functions (FUN_007fa320, FUN_0070fa70, FUN_00561a80, sub_007f99b0.blk_007f99b0) with no dominant one.
A limiter that sleeps would show as idle time; a limiter that spins would show as one hot function. Neither is present.
no_frame_cap_to_remove.conclusion: The frame costs about 41 ms of guest simulation work that is largely independent of the draw count, with the draw path added on top in heavier scenes. There is nothing to unlock: 60 FPS at this scene would need the guest's work to be about 2.5x faster. That was not achieved and is not claimed.

The counts are measured; their cost in milliseconds is not, so they are a candidate to reduce and not a demonstrated gain.
